regulator: Agence sénégalaise de Réglementation pharmaceutique (ARP) – https://arp.sn

facts.title: Regulator and legal basis
facts.body: The ARP registers medicines under Law 2023-06 of 13 June 2023 on medicines, other health products and pharmacy (art. 133: no medicine may be supplied in Senegal without a marketing authorisation, the AMM, granted by ministerial order) and the UEMOA regulation 04/2020/CM/UEMOA on the homologation of human medicines. WHO rated the ARP at Maturity Level 3 in 2026, the first francophone African regulator to reach it. Applications are filed online on the ARP's Portail Homologation.

facts.title: CTD dossier in the UEMOA format, in French
facts.body: The dossier follows the UEMOA Common Technical Document (modules 1 to 5, annexes to regulation 04/2020). Module 1 is country specific; modules 2 to 5 are shared across UEMOA states, so one technical dossier serves Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Togo, Benin and Guinea-Bissau. The dossier and labelling are in French. A dossier found incomplete at screening gets three months to be completed.

facts.title: 120 days of regulatory time, 360 days at most
facts.body: The UEMOA regulation sets the review of a new AMM, a variation or a renewal at 120 days of regulatory time, with a ceiling of 360 days. The clock stops while the applicant answers questions from screening or the expert committee. In practice the ARP's technical committee sits in sessions (118 dossiers reviewed in one five-day session in November 2025), so the time between sessions adds to the wait.

facts.title: Abridged dossier for WHO-prequalified products
facts.body: Products prequalified by WHO are assessed on an abridged dossier under the collaborative procedure between the country and WHO: the ARP obtains WHO's assessment report and may ask for modules 4 and 5 only when needed. All other products, including those for tropical or neglected diseases, file a full dossier.

facts.title: Fees for a foreign manufacturer (decree 2025-1833)
facts.body: Decree 2025-1833 of 18 November 2025 (Journal officiel of 29 December 2025) sets the ARP's fees. For foreign industry: registration of a generic 1,000,000 FCFA, of an originator 1,500,000 FCFA, registration under the accelerated procedure 2,000,000 FCFA, renewal 500,000 FCFA (late renewal: 1% of the renewal fee per day), major variation 1,000,000 FCFA, minor variation 150,000 FCFA (originator) or 100,000 FCFA (generic). Local industry pays half or less (registration 500,000 FCFA). An AMM and its renewal run five years.

facts.title: GMP certificate of the manufacturing site
facts.body: The ARP issues or renews a good manufacturing practice certificate for each site. Decree 2025-1833 prices it by where the site is: outside Africa 8,000,000 FCFA for an on-site inspection or 3,000,000 FCFA for a desk review or virtual inspection; elsewhere in Africa 5,500,000 / 2,000,000 FCFA; in ECOWAS 4,000,000 / 1,500,000 FCFA; a local site 1,500,000 FCFA. Good distribution practice certificates for wholesalers follow the same pattern (1,000,000 FCFA local).

facts.title: Sample import authorisation
facts.body: Registration samples enter under an import authorisation of 100,000 FCFA per product, form and strength, valid six months (decree 2025-1833).

facts.title: Import levy and duty-free entry
facts.body: Medicines sit in category 0 of the ECOWAS common external tariff (no customs duty); the UEMOA community levy (0.8%), the ECOWAS levy (0.5%) and the statistical fee (1%) still apply. Decree 2025-1833 adds an annual levy of 0.10% of the value of medicine imports. Medicines are exempt from the 18% VAT under the General Tax Code.

facts.title: Regulated public prices
facts.body: Public prices of medicines are set by ministerial order through coefficients on the CIF price (interministerial order 000188/MSHP/DPM of 15 January 2003: about 1.85 for ordinary medicines, lower for 'social' medicines; generics sold by the national supply pharmacy SEN-PNA at PNA price times 1.5). The 2003 order is still the reference cited; check the current schedule with the ARP before pricing.

facts.title: Public register, five-year validity, medical representatives
facts.body: Every AMM is published in the ARP's open database (medicine, INN, strength, form, route, laboratory, therapeutic class; 7,458 entries in October 2026). An AMM is valid five years and renewed at 500,000 FCFA. Each medical representative is registered with the ARP (50,000 FCFA, two years); advertising needs an authorisation per medium (100,000 FCFA a year).

routes.label: Full review (UEMOA national procedure)
routes.description: Default route for an imported generic or originator: UEMOA CTD in French on the Portail Homologation, screening, expert committee, national commission, ministerial order. 120 days of regulatory time, 360 at most, plus the clock stops; committee sessions set the pace. Fee 1,000,000 FCFA for a generic, 1,500,000 FCFA for an originator (about USD 1,700 to 2,550), plus the GMP certificate of the site.

routes.label: Accelerated procedure
routes.description: The fee decree prices an accelerated registration at 2,000,000 FCFA (about USD 3,400) for foreign industry. The ARP decides which dossiers qualify (public-health priority, products already approved by a stringent authority); ask before filing.

routes.label: WHO prequalification (abridged dossier)
routes.description: A WHO-prequalified product files an abridged dossier under the collaborative procedure; the ARP relies on WHO's assessment report and may still ask for modules 4 and 5. Faster than the full review; same fee as the full procedure.
